heroHeadline: One Month On, Madrid Unveils €165M Ceuta Package as Security Chief Takes Direct Command Amid Rising Community Tension
heroSubtitle: Marking a month since the mass crossing, Spain's Council of Ministers approved a €165 million emergency economic package for Ceuta while Secretary of State for Security Aina Calvo relocated to the city to personally oversee accommodation and returns, under a command now chaired by PM Pedro Sánchez, with a two-week target to clear migrants from the streets. Nightly unrest continues, with reports emerging of Muslim residents being targeted by protesters for helping migrants, raising fears of a religious divide in a city long proud of its Christian-Muslim coexistence. PP leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo is making Ceuta the centerpiece of the political season's opening, organizing nationwide September 2 protests ahead of Sánchez's planned September 3 Congress appearance, while a new media retrospective puts the crossing's death toll above 150 — the highest figure reported to date.
